## ✨ Highlights

- 🪞 **Updates when the image factory can't be reached**: a node with extensions gets its update from the image factory; when janus.sw-servers.net is down, the Controller now asks its mirror, `janus-mirror.sw-servers.net` - a read-only copy, hosted elsewhere, of the update bundles the factory built for its two newest releases ([#417](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/417), [#420](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/420), [When the factory can't be reached](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/image-factory.md#when-the-factory-cant-be-reached-its-mirror)).
- 📊 **An opt-in usage report**: once a day, if an admin turns it on - an unticked box at setup, **Settings › Usage report** -, how many nodes and clusters the Controller manages, their versions, extensions, variants, sizes and the features in use; never a name, an address or a configuration, and no IP address kept on the other side. It decides what to work on, what could be retired, and which images to pre-build first ([#419](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/419), [Usage report](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/telemetry.md)).
- 📈 **Download counts on the image builder**: each platform, HAProxy branch, kernel track, console and extension shows how often it was downloaded in the last 30 days - images and updates, counted without anything about who ([#416](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/416)).
- 🔗 **Every site a node routes reaches Consul, even behind a socket**: a frontend that listens only on `abns@`/`unix@` - the usual TCP `:443` that splits TLS by server name and hands it to an HTTP frontend - now gets its URLs at the bind relaying to it. A production node set up that way had registered 1 URL of its 30 ([#412](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/412)).
- 🏷️ **Tags to pick services by**: `scheme=https`, `proto=http`/`proto=tcp` on the URLs, frontends and exporters, and `scheme`, `proto`, `host` in their meta - `tags: [url, proto=http]` in Prometheus ([#412](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/412), [The node's services](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/consul-controller.md#the-nodes-services)).
- 🩺 **A frontend's health is HAProxy's own**: no more connection from the node to each frontend - a frontend that refuses other sources flapped between passing and critical ([#412](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/412)).
- 🔁 **janusd always comes back**: on a node booted from an update that waited for its health - every update the Controller makes -, janusd exiting once the update was confirmed (a Restart, a crash) was never started again: the node lost its API, and its extensions, until a reboot ([#415](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/415)).

What the production rollout of v2026.10.29-3 and the consul extension found ([its lab pass](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/pre-release-tests/v2026.10.29-3.md), [#409](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/409), found nothing new).

## 🔄 Since the v2026.10.29-5 pre-release

- **The image factory's mirror** and the Controller asking it ([#417](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/417), [#420](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/420)), **the usage report** ([#419](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/419)) and **the builder's download counts** ([#416](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/416)) - the sections below.

## 🔄 Since the v2026.10.29-4 pre-release

What [its lab pass](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/pre-release-tests/v2026.10.29-4.md) found ([#414](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/414)):

- **janusd restarted after an update's confirmation** ([#415](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/415)) - since `wait_for_health` came (2026-09-24): a boot with an update to confirm gives init a deadline (60 s, or the update's health timeout) after which a janusd that can't stay up reverts the update. Past it, janusd's first exit found the update confirmed - nothing to revert - and init stopped supervising it: `init: /sbin/janusd (pid …) exited (0)`, then nothing. HAProxy served on; the API, and the extensions janusd had stopped (bird, keepalived, consul…), were gone until a reboot. init now goes back to restarting janusd forever (`init: this boot is confirmed - janusd is restarted as on any boot`).
- **Prometheus's `filter` doesn't pick URLs**: it picks services from Consul's catalog, not their instances - `ServiceMeta.proto == "tcp"` kept every `haproxy-url`. The guide says to use `tags: [url, proto=…]`, or a `keep` on `__meta_consul_service_metadata_proto` ([#415](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/415)).

## 🧭 Consul

- **URLs of a frontend behind a socket** ([#412](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/412)): a frontend whose binds are all sockets (`abns@`, `unix@`, a path, the loopback) was skipped - no URL of its maps or Host ACLs was registered.
  - Its URLs now take the address and port of the frontend that relays to it: one whose backend - `use_backend`, `default_backend`, a dynamic rule's map values, a listen section - has a server on one of its sockets. Chains are followed up to 4 hops.
  - https when either bind has `ssl`. Their meta's `via` names the relaying frontend.
  - A host the relay also routes by SNI is registered once.
  - The socket-only frontend gets no `haproxy-<frontend>` service of its own: the relay's sits at that address already.
- **key=value tags** ([#412](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/412)) - beside the tags v2026.10.29-3 gave, kept:
  - `haproxy-url`: `scheme=http|https` and `proto=http|tcp` - `http` for a host routed by its Host header, `tcp` for TLS passed on by its SNI - and meta `scheme`, `proto`, `host`.
  - `haproxy-<frontend>`: `proto=` its mode, `scheme=https` when a bind has `ssl` (`scheme=http` for an HTTP frontend without).
  - `janus-exporter`, `node-exporter`, `haproxy-exporter`: `scheme=`.
  - The Prometheus example's blackbox job probes `tags: [url, proto=http]`.
- **A frontend's check is HAProxy's state of it** ([#412](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/412)): `haproxy-<frontend>` and `haproxy-exporter` had a TCP check - a connection from the node itself, which a frontend refusing other sources (`tcp-request connection reject unless { src … }`) reset at once: passing or critical by chance. They now have a TTL check janusd feeds from the frontend's row in `show stat` every 15 s - `OPEN` passing, `FULL` warning, `STOP` or no row critical, with its sessions in the output -; a janusd that stops lets it expire (60 s). `janus` keeps its TCP check, the exporters their HTTP checks.

## 🪞 The image factory and its mirror

- **The Controller asks the mirror when the factory can't be reached** ([#417](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/417)): no connection, no answer within 10 seconds, or a 5xx - the same question goes to `janus-mirror.sw-servers.net` (`GET /api/v1/updates/<id>`, the same answer). For a node's **Update** page - whose Source line then says "the image factory's mirror" -, a machine's version change and a cluster's update alike; the node, or the Controller's relay, downloads the bundle from the mirror. A refusal from the factory is its answer: the mirror isn't asked. A new machine's disk image never comes from the mirror.
- **What it holds**: the update bundles the factory built for its two newest releases - never a pre-release, nor a disk image -, copied every 15 minutes, each file checked against the factory's SHA-256 ([#420](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/420)). It builds nothing: a schematic nobody had built isn't there. The node checks the bundle's SHA-256 and its UKIs' signature wherever it comes from - the mirror needs no more trust than the factory.
- `dashboardd -image-factory-mirror` / `JANUS_CONTROLLER_IMAGE_FACTORY_MIRROR`: `auto`, the default, is this mirror with the default `-image-factory`, none with another; empty, none.
- **Download counts** ([#416](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/416)): the builder's choices show their downloads of the last 30 days; `GET /api/v1/stats/downloads?days=N` gives them by platform, release, branch, track, console and extension - never by schematic. The default schematic's updates come from GitHub's own counts; the mirror sends its own. The factory keeps a schematic's builds of its three newest **releases** - pre-releases no longer push one out.
- **Pre-builds in the order nodes run them**: when a release comes out, the schematics the usage reports name most are built first ([#420](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/420)).

## 📊 Usage report

- **Opt-in, once a day** ([#419](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/419)): off until an admin turns it on - the setup screen's unticked box, or **Settings › Usage report** -, then within the hour (a moment its ID picks), then every 24 hours; a failure is tried again an hour later.
- **Counts only**: nodes (total, not answering, by version, architecture, HAProxy branch, kernel track, console, extension, schematic, size bucket), clusters and their sizes, machines by kind of hypervisor, and features on or off. Never a name, an address, a label or a configuration. **Exactly what is sent** in the card shows the report as it would leave.
- **Its ID** is 128 random bits, apart from the Controller's own; **New ID** makes another and asks the receiver to delete what it holds under the old one. **Send now** sends one at once.
- `JANUS_CONTROLLER_TELEMETRY=off` keeps it off whatever the page says; `JANUS_CONTROLLER_TELEMETRY_URL` sends it elsewhere.
- The setup screen's checkboxes keep their size when their text wraps - the second factor's had shrunk to a dot.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **A cluster member's update is found before the member is drained** ([#411](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/411)): a Controller that reaches the image factory through the cluster's own address lost its connection when the member's routes moved, and the update stopped - harmlessly. The bundle is now found, and a factory build waited for, while the member still serves; a failure there leaves it in service.
- **A machine is ready with what it runs** ([#411](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/411)): after an update its record said the old version for a moment, and a Terraform apply failed with "Provider produced inconsistent result after apply" (`.version`) - the update was done, the next plan clean.
- **An update error that's behind the machine goes** ([#411](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/411)): a machine whose update failed - a node that can't reach the factory - kept "update failed" after its node was updated another way (the bundle pushed from its page). The history now says the failed update is superseded.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **A network that lets the nodes and the Controller reach chosen hosts only**: add `janus-mirror.sw-servers.net` beside `janus.sw-servers.net` and `github.com` for the updates, and `janus-telemetry.sw-servers.net` for the Controller if you turn the usage report on.
- **The usage report stays off** on an updated Controller until an admin turns it on; `JANUS_CONTROLLER_TELEMETRY=off` locks it off.
- **The nodes need this release** for the URLs, tags and checks - and for janusd to come back after an exit: update them. Until then, on a node updated by the Controller, reboot it rather than Restart janusd. Their frontends' checks become TTL checks - something reading the check's type or output sees the change.
- **The Prometheus example now filters `proto=http`**: a job copied from it leaves out the URLs passed on by SNI (`proto=tcp`) - drop the filter to keep probing them.
